data.title: Stock market slips as 10-year Treasury yield tops 5% ahead of Fed decision
data.description:
Wall Street opened lower on Tuesday while Treasury yields rose as traders looked forward to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision later in the week.

The S&P 500 (SP500) -0.1%, the Dow (DJI) -0.2%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) -0.2%.

The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield (US10Y) climbed to its highest level in nearly two decades, extending a global bond selloff driven by surging energy prices, rising debt, and inflation concerns.

The bond-market selloff adds pressure ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision Wednesday, with investors expecting officials to raise short-term borrowing costs for the first time since July 2023.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) rose 1.8 basis points to 4.69%, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) rose 1 basis point to 5.01%, and the 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) rose 4.7 basis points to 5.40%.

On the economic calendar, investors will monitor the 20-year bond auction.

data.title: Cabot appoints interim CFO
data.description:
• Cabot Corporation (CBT) has appointed Steve Delahunt, vice president and corporate treasurer, to serve as chief financial officer on an interim basis, effective October 1, 2026.

  • Erica McLaughlin, currently executive vice president, chief financial officer and head of Corporate Strategy, has been elected president and chief executive officer of Cabot, effective October 1, 2026, succeeding Sean Keohane.

  • McLaughlin will step down from her position as chief financial officer at that time.

data.title: The AI safety bill rally is already unraveling
data.description:
The odds of the U.S. passing an AI safety bill before 2027 have fallen sharply on Polymarket, even as warnings about the risks of advanced artificial intelligence have intensified in Washington and Silicon Valley.

Polymarket data showed the probability at 17% on Sept. 15, down from a spike to about 45% on Sept. 10. The one-week chart showed the sharp jump came after reports that a bipartisan group of senators was working on legislation aimed at imposing safety requirements on developers of advanced AI models.

A bipartisan AI safety bill from senators Amy Klobuchar, Ted Cruz, and John Thune may be introduced as early as next week, Semafor reported, citing unnamed sources.

The proposed legislation is still being negotiated and would seek to make AI companies responsible for addressing potentially catastrophic risks from their systems. Among the ideas discussed is a legal “duty of care” for developers, requiring them to design AI systems with safeguards against major risks, Reuters reported. 

The push for legislation has gained urgency following a series of warnings from AI researchers and industry executives. OpenAI (OPEAI) has advocated mandatory national safety requirements based on the capabilities of advanced models, including outside testing, cybersecurity protections, and incident reporting. CEO Sam Altman endorsed the idea and said his company would also grant independent evaluators employee-like access.

The debate has also been fueled by increasingly stark warnings about whether advanced AI could ultimately threaten human survival. Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic (ANTHRO) researcher, resigned this month and warned that people building advanced AI believe it could potentially kill humans by the end of the decade.

Anthropic alignment researcher Evan Hubinger separately put the probability of AI causing human extinction within the next decade at more than 10%, a personal estimate rather than a scientific consensus.

Anthropic (ANTHRO) CEO Dario Amodei called for deliberately slowing improvements in the most powerful AI systems so that safety research and oversight can catch up. 

Amodei has also called for the industry to slow the pace of AI development, warning that AI agents could potentially gain the ability to control large parts of the internet within six to 12 months if safeguards fail to keep up. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk have backed the need for greater caution.

The warnings have put pressure on lawmakers to act, but the political path remains uncertain. Senate Majority Leader John Thune has backed congressional involvement and is working with Democrats and Republicans on possible legislation.

House Speaker Mike Johnson said Congress should consult the leaders of the nation’s largest artificial intelligence companies before moving ahead with broad federal regulations, arguing that lawmakers cannot afford to rush legislation governing the rapidly advancing technology.

President Donald Trump has meanwhile dismissed concerns over AI risks and opposed what he sees as excessive regulation.

With Congress facing a crowded schedule ahead of the November midterm elections, the prediction market is now pricing in less than a one-in-five chance that an AI safety bill will become law before 2027.

data.title: Arthur J. Gallagher buys McMillan Insurance & Bonding
data.description:
• Arthur J. Gallagher (AJG) has acquired Englewood, Colorado-based McMillan Insurance & Bonding, dba Innovise Business Consultants.
  • Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
  • Innovise Business Consultants provides commercial insurance brokerage and surety bonding services with industry focuses of construction, energy, real estate, and manufacturing.
  • The Innovise Business Consultants team, led by Jason McMillan, will relocate to Gallagher (AJG)'s Denver office under the direction of Bret VanderVoort, head of Gallagher's Western Zone retail property/casualty brokerage operations.

data.title: Worldwide NFT signs LOI to acquire RedTrace Technologies
data.description:
• Worldwide NFT (WNFT) has signed a letter of intent to acquire 100% of the capital stock of RedTrace Technologies, a Maryland-based provider of cybersecurity services to the United States government.
  • RedTrace generates several million dollars in annual revenue and positive run-rate EBITDA.
  • The LOI is expected to close in the 4th calendar quarter of 2026.

data.title: Charles Schwab core net new assets rise 12% M/M, 46% Y/Y in August
data.description:
Charles Schwab's (SCHW) core net new assets of $64.8B climbed 12% M/M and 46% Y/Y, the company said Tuesday.

Total client assets at the end of the month were $13.4T, up 3% M/M and 19% Y/Y.  By comparison, the S&P 500 Index (SPX) increased 3% M/M and 19% Y/Y.

Client daily average trades were 9.82M, down 16% M/M and up 37% Y/Y. Margin balances at the end of the month, though, were $177.6B, rising 5% M/M and 92% Y/Y.

The number of active brokerage accounts, at 49.1M, increased 6% Y/Y.

Transactional sweep cash at the end of August stood at $483.3B, up 1% M/M and 19% Y/Y, driven by continued client demand for long/short strategies, the company said.

Charles Schwab (SCHW) stock rose 0.6% in premarket trading.

data.title: Broadcom’s strong AI growth faces margin, financing risks
data.description:
Broadcom’s (AVGO) strong AI revenue growth is being accompanied by mounting margin and financing concerns as the cost of components and supply constraints weigh on the semiconductor company, according to Joe Albano of Tech Cache. 

While Broadcom’s AI business continues to accelerate, Albano said the company is facing margin compression as higher DRAM, NAND and other component costs increase pressure across the AI infrastructure supply chain.

Albano said Broadcom’s outlook reflects strong demand for its custom AI accelerators, or XPUs, but cautioned that the broader financing structure behind the AI buildout warrants attention. With demand backing up in a supply-constrained environment, Broadcom’s guidance extending into fiscal 2028 is not necessarily surprising, he said.

However, the longer-term question is whether the companies funding AI infrastructure can continue supporting such high levels of spending if the anticipated returns from AI take longer to materialize.

A key concern for Albano is the increasingly interconnected financing model surrounding AI infrastructure. He pointed to the use of custom chips as collateral in some financing arrangements and questioned how fungible those assets would be if an AI customer were to run into financial difficulties.

Because custom XPUs are designed around specific customer workloads, their value could be less straightforward outside their original applications, potentially creating additional risks if funding conditions deteriorate.

The concerns come even as Broadcom benefits from the continued expansion of AI infrastructure spending. Albano's broader view is that investors need to look beyond headline revenue growth and consider whether the enormous capital being committed to AI can ultimately produce sustainable cash flows.

With major technology companies and AI labs committing increasingly large sums to infrastructure, the ability of the ecosystem to keep financing that spending could become a more important issue over the coming year.

For Broadcom, Albano remains cautious despite the strong underlying AI demand. He said the company could face a more difficult environment if the financing supporting AI infrastructure begins to weaken, particularly if expectations around the arrival of artificial general intelligence are pushed further out.

The result, in his view, is a stock where strong AI demand needs to be weighed against the sustainability of the spending and financing cycle supporting that demand.

data.title: Mach Natural Resources holder to offer shares for up to $11.90 each - Bloomberg
data.description:
Mach Natural Resources (MNR) falls 9.5% pre-market Tuesday following a Bloomberg report that shareholder Kayne Anderson is offering shares in the company for $11.60-$11.90 each in an unregistered block trade, with Morgan Stanley reportedly serving as the sole book-running manager.

Kayne Anderson's offering of 8M shares of Mach Natural Resources (MNR) would be marketed at as much as a 7.1% discount to Monday’s $12.49 closing price.

The offering comes as Mach Natural Resources (MNR) is coping with high debt levels and heavy exposure to weak natural gas prices.

data.title: Semiconductor TAM set to double by 2030 to $3.2T on memory and data center demand: BofA
data.description:
Although it took the semiconductor industry 50 years to reach the $1T mark in annual sales, the sector is currently growing at an incredible rate due to near-insatiable demand.

Bank of America has forecast the total addressable market for the semiconductor industry to nearly double from $1.7T in 2026 to $3.2T by 2030. The growth is mostly due to memory and data centers as well as an incremental recovery in the auto and industrial sectors. 

"Despite rising concerns around potential AI infra/investment slowdown, we see no signs of slowing in customer orders, LTAs, capacity commitments, or semis pricing (memory/GPU rental)," said BofA analysts, led by Vivek Arya, in an industry report. "For instance, latest memory pricing is flattish week-on-week for both DRAM/NAND, and the latest GPU rental pricing for NVDA's (NVDA) B200 is $5.72/hr, up consistently over the last two months and only <10% below the ~$6.10 peak from March."

AMD (AMD) also indicated that they are not identifying any signs of customer orders slowing down.

"2027 remains much a fully booked/contracted year across all compute/networking/memory vendors, and we expect 2028 to also remain tight, led by accelerating demand for CPUs, XPU attach, and new optics-based scale-up, as well as accelerating AI accelerator business at multiple ASIC and GPU vendors," Arya added.

Although the sector as a whole might remain rangebound in the near term, BofA highlights several stocks that should show more resilience. This includes Nvidia and AMD for compute, Marvell (MRVL) for networking, and Analog Devices (ADI) and onsemi (ON) for analog. And, if momentum returns, Micron (MU), Lam Research (LRCX), Applied Materials (AMAT) and Intel (INTC) could lead in gains.

BofA broke down the forecasted growth by segment to reach the potential $3.2T in sales by 2030 from 2026. Memory is set to grow to $1.8T from $937B, core semis to $1.35T from $739B, servers to $848B from $359B, PCs to $68.7B from $55.8B, smartphones to $77.8B from $71.1B, automotive to $90B from $60B, industrial to $99B from $65B, and the "Other" category, which includes storage, wired, wireless infra and consumer, to $166B from $127B.

Over the same period, spending on wafer fabrication equipment is forecast to increase to $359.8B from $155.9B.

data.title: 4 stocks to watch on Tuesday: JNJ, NYT, AAPL, and ETSY
data.description:
Stock index futures were lower on Tuesday while Treasury yields rose as traders looked forward to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision later in the week.

Here are four stocks to watch on the day: 

Etsy (ETSY) gained 3.28% in premarket trade after Oppenheimer upgraded the stock to Outperform from Perform and set a $90 price target, representing 21% upside to Monday’s closing price. Analyst Jason Helfstein said product improvements are reducing Etsy’s dependence on Google Search as consumers increasingly use AI, while a survey of 2,500 U.S. consumers supported the view that the changes are working. Oppenheimer raised its FY26 GMS estimate to a street-high 1%, with 5% GMS growth projected for FY27 and FY28, including anticipated share losses to new entrants in the online handmade market.

The New York Times Company (NYT) rose 1.31% in early action after Guggenheim upgraded the stock to Buy from Neutral and lifted its price target to $82 from $70, citing a more attractive valuation and confidence in sustained digital advertising and subscription growth. Analyst Michael Morris and his team said the company can sustain “low-double-digit digital advertising growth” through 2027 despite tougher comparisons, supported by demand across its News, Sports, Games, and Shopping properties, as well as additional inventory and video monetization opportunities.

Apple (AAPL) slipped 0.57% in premarket trade after India’s consumer regulator began examining the company’s software warranty terms as part of an investigation into allegations that the iOS 18 update damaged iPhone functionality and forced users to pay “exorbitant” repair costs, Reuters reported Tuesday. The investigation adds to Apple’s challenges in India, where the company is expanding iPhone manufacturing and gaining market share while also facing accusations of breaching domestic antitrust laws.

Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) edged 0.14% lower in early action after reporting new Phase 2b COPERNICUS study results showing that less-frequent dosing and preventive strategies with RYBREVANT FASPRO and LAZCLUZE could improve the treatment experience for patients with previously untreated advanced non-small cell lung cancer carrying common EGFR mutations. The company said subcutaneous treatment and prophylaxis were associated with low rates of rash, blood clots, and administration-related reactions.
